title: Turn on lost-phone settings before you need them
summary: Find My iPhone, Google Find Hub and Samsung Find have critical tracking settings to enable now, before your phone ever goes missing or stolen.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You know that awful feeling when you reach for your phone, and it is suddenly nowhere to be found. Maybe you left it at a restaurant. Maybe it slipped between the car seats. Or maybe somebody walked away with it. The worst time to start figuring out your phone's tracking features is after it disappears. Fortunately, iPhone, Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones include powerful tools that can help you locate a missing device and protect the information stored on it. Take a few minutes while your phone is still safely in your hand and make sure these settings are ready.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT
Turn on your phone’s lost-device and theft protections now, so you are ready to locate it and protect your data if it disappears. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
Turn on Find My iPhone in iOS 27

Apple's Find My system can help locate an iPhone when it is online. With the right settings enabled, supported iPhones can also remain findable when they are offline or for a period after they have been turned off.
Open SettingsTap your nameTap Find MyTap Find My iPhoneTurn on Find My iPhoneTurn on Find My networkTurn on Send Last Location
Open Settings
Tap your name
Tap Find My
Tap Find My iPhone
Turn on Find My iPhone
Turn on Find My network
Turn on Send Last Location

Find My network lets nearby Apple devices securely help locate your iPhone when it cannot connect to Wi-Fi or cellular service. On supported iPhones, Apple says the Find My network can locate the phone for up to 24 hours after it is turned off or up to five hours while it is in power reserve mode. Meanwhile, Send Last Location automatically sends your iPhone's location to Apple when its battery reaches a critically low level. That could give you one more place to check if the battery dies before you realize your phone is missing.

While you are there, I would check another iPhone security feature called Stolen Device Protection. Open Settings > Face ID & Passcode and enter your passcode. Tap Stolen Device Protection, then make sure it is turned on. By default, Apple applies its added security requirements when your iPhone is away from familiar locations such as home or work. You can make those protections stronger by choosing Always under Require Security Delay. Stolen Device Protection can require Face ID or Touch ID for sensitive actions. Certain account changes can also trigger a one-hour Security Delay followed by another biometric check. Find My cannot be turned off while Stolen Device Protection is enabled. That extra hurdle can be especially useful if someone steals your iPhone and has also seen or learned your passcode.
STOLEN IPHONES FUEL SCARY PASSCODE SCAM
iPhone owners can use Apple’s Find My network to help locate a missing device even when it goes offline. (Apple)
Google Pixel owners should check Find Hub

Google now calls its lost-device service Find Hub. If you have added a Google Account to your Pixel, Find Hub is usually enabled automatically. Still, I would check these settings before you ever need them.
Open SettingsTap Security & privacyTap Lost device protectionTap Find HubMake sure Allow device to be located is turned onTap Find your offline devicesChoose the offline-finding option you prefer
Open Settings
Tap Security & privacy
Tap Lost device protection
Tap Find Hub
Make sure Allow device to be located is turned on
Tap Find your offline devices
Choose the offline-finding option you prefer
For the broadest coverage, choose With network everywhere if that option appears on your Pixel. This lets nearby Android devices help locate your phone when it cannot connect normally.

You should also open Settings > Location and make sure Use location is turned on. Google recommends setting a PIN, pattern or password too. A screen lock helps your Pixel use Find Hub's end-to-end encrypted offline-finding network. Supported newer Pixel phones can also remain findable through Find Hub for several hours after the battery runs out or the phone is powered off. For that feature to work, Bluetooth, Location and offline finding should be enabled before the phone shuts down.

Go to Settings > Security & privacy > Lost device protection. From there, review the additional theft safeguards available on your Pixel. Depending on your device and software version, you may see Theft Detection Lock, Offline Device Lock, Remote Lock and Identity Check. These features can automatically lock your phone in certain situations or require biometric authentication before sensitive account changes are made. Find Hub helps you locate the phone, while these additional protections can help secure it if someone takes it.
Pixel owners can use Google Find Hub and offline finding to help track down a phone when it loses its normal connection. (Google)
Samsung Galaxy owners have two finding systems
If you use a Samsung Galaxy phone, you can take advantage of both Google Find Hub and Samsung's own device-finding tools.
Open SettingsTap Security and privacyTap Lost device protectionTap Find My MobileTurn on Allow this phone to be foundTurn on Send last locationTurn on Offline finding
Open Settings
Tap Security and privacy
Tap Lost device protection
Tap Find My Mobile
Turn on Allow this phone to be found
Turn on Send last location
Turn on Offline finding

You will need a Samsung account on the phone to use Samsung Find and SmartThings Find. Send last location can preserve the phone's last known location. Offline finding lets nearby Galaxy devices help update the location when your phone cannot connect normally. Samsung says that if the phone is powered off, you may only see its last known location. That makes turning these protections on ahead of time especially useful.

I would keep Google Find Hub available on a Samsung phone as well. Samsung's current instructions say you can verify it by opening Settings > Google Services > Find Hub > tap on your device > Settings and checking that Allow device to be located is turned on. That gives Galaxy owners another way to locate or secure a missing phone through their Google Account. You may see slightly different wording depending on your Galaxy model, carrier or software version. Samsung notes that some menus can vary between devices.
Galaxy owners can use Samsung Find alongside Google Find Hub to help locate and secure a missing phone. (Samsung)
What to do when your phone actually disappears
If an iPhone goes missing, open Find My on another Apple device or use Apple's Find Devices service through iCloud.com. From there, you can view the phone on a map, play a sound or mark it as lost.

Google Pixel and other Android owners can open the Find Hub app on another Android device or use Google's Find Hub through a web browser. You can locate the phone, play a sound or mark it as lost. You can also erase the device remotely if recovery looks unlikely.
Samsung Galaxy owners can use Samsung Find or SmartThings Find through their Samsung account in addition to Google Find Hub.

If the phone appears to be sitting somewhere nearby, playing a sound can save you from tearing the house apart. However, if the map shows your phone somewhere unfamiliar and you suspect it was stolen, avoid trying to recover it yourself. Contact law enforcement instead.
Watch out for scams after your phone is stolen

Losing the phone can also open the door to another problem. Thieves have used convincing Apple-style texts and fake Find My websites to trick stolen iPhone owners into revealing their passcodes. A message may claim that your missing phone has suddenly been found and include a link where you can supposedly see its location. Avoid tapping those links. Instead, open Find My yourself or go directly to Apple's official Find Devices service. The same basic rule applies to Android. If a message claims your missing device has been located, open Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly rather than signing in through a link somebody sent you.

Pro tip: Use strong antivirus software. Strong security software can help warn you about malicious links, phishing sites and other online threats that may appear after your phone is stolen. It adds another layer of protection, but you should still avoid clicking unexpected messages claiming your missing phone has been found. Instead, open Find My, Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
A few minutes now can save a lot of panic later

Most of us do not think much about these settings while our phone is sitting safely in our hand. Then the phone disappears and suddenly every one of them becomes very important. I would check them now. Make sure your phone can be located, make sure offline finding is enabled and confirm that you know which account you would need to sign in to from another device. You may never need any of these features. If you do, you will already know where to start.
Kurt's key takeaways

Your phone already has some impressive tools for finding it, but those tools work best when you prepare before the phone goes missing. On an iPhone, I would make sure Find My network and Send Last Location are enabled. Pixel owners should check Find Hub and offline finding, while Galaxy users can add Samsung's Lost device protection on top of Google's system. I would also spend another minute reviewing the theft protections available on your phone. Apple's Stolen Device Protection and Google's theft protection features can make it harder for someone who gets your phone to take control of your accounts. That extra layer could become incredibly valuable when you are already dealing with the stress of a missing device.
If your phone disappeared right now, would you know exactly how to find and protect it, or would you be learning these settings for the first time? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Transgender Washington state resident accused of fueling deadly Canadian school massacre that killed 8: DOJ
summary: James Cody Bryant allegedly sent money, offered advice and agreed to livestream the Tumbler Ridge school shooting instead of alerting law enforcement.
story: Federal officials say James Cody Bryant sent money, offered advice and agreed to livestream the Canadian school shooting that killed eight victims. (Credit: U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington)

A transgender Washington state resident allegedly helped fuel a Canadian school massacre that left children dead, choosing to aid the shooter, who also identified as a transgender, instead of sounding the alarm, federal officials said Tuesday.

James Cody Bryant, 30, was arrested Tuesday morning in Bellingham north of Seattle, accused of sending money, offering advice and agreeing to broadcast the Feb. 10 attack at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia.

"Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement, and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to," Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said at a Seattle news conference.
"Instead, he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer."
TRANSGEDNER EX-STUDENT IDENTIFIED AS ALLEGED SUSPECT IN DEADLY CANADA SCHOOL MASS SHOOTING

U.S. and Canadian officials discuss the arrest of James Cody Bryant, 30, in connection with the deadly Tumbler Ridge school shooting during a news conference Tuesday in Seattle. (U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington)

Bryant faces a federal charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Prosecutors allege Bryant helped the shooter, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, start a car to reach the school after the killings had begun.

"So even after the shooter had already tragically killed two family members, Bryant assisted the shooter in successfully traveling to the second location to take even more lives," FBI Seattle Special Agent in Charge W. Mike Herrington said.
"In the complaint, Bryant even admits to being maybe the only one who could stop the shooter."
Herrington confirmed that Bryant and Van Rootselaar both identified as transgender, and said Bryant identifies as female.
The two met through a random pairing on the online chat service Omegle roughly three years before the attack.
Investigators have no indication what their transgender identities were, why they remained in contact, or that they ever met in person, Herrington said.
TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL

Police tape surrounds the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and other buildings in Tumbler Ridge, Vancouver, British Columbia, Feb. 11, the day after a mass shooting there. (Jesse Boily /The Canadian Press via AP, File)
Their online friendship developed into discussions of violence over at least six months, according to Herrington.
"This complaint was particularly difficult to read, in part because of the casual tone these two individuals used when discussing the mass taking of innocent lives that was being planned," he said.
Bryant allegedly agreed to record and broadcast a livestream to maximize the shooter’s notoriety.
"Bryant even stayed awake after an overnight work shift to make sure this horrific act could be widely viewed online," Herrington said.
FLORIDA MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY PLOTTING MASS SHOOTING TARGETING JEWISH EMPLOYEES AT ADVOCACY ORGANIZATION

Police officers and investigators work outside Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where a mass shooting took place in the small town of Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Canada, on Feb. 10. (Eagle Vision Agency / AFP via Getty Images, File)

"We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the livestream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the livestream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

Floyd said the attempted livestream on Twitch lasted about 20 seconds before shutting down. Herrington said investigators do not know whether Van Rootselaar would have carried out the attack without Bryant’s willingness to operate it.
Officials also described financial assistance, including a little more than $100 for shoes. An attempted transfer of roughly $15 for a lighter was ultimately reversed.
NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

Community members mourn during a candlelight vigil for the victims of Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where a mass shooting took place in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Feb. 10. (Paige Taylor White / AFP via Getty Images, File)

Floyd said Bryant and the shooter discussed sending weapons to Canada, but Bryant was uncomfortable doing so. Herrington said investigators had no indication the guns used in the attack came from the U.S.
Asked about a possible political ideology or group affiliation, Floyd said investigators had no information indicating either.

Herrington pointed to the shooter’s suffering and "a very keen focus on notoriety" as themes in the communications. The pair discussed other mass shootings, how the public reacted and a desire for the Tumbler Ridge attack to receive similar attention, he said.

The investigation crossed the border within days of the massacre, when Canadian police received information from an online platform used by the shooter and contacted the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), British Columbia RCMP Assistant Commissioner Elija Rain said.
Floyd said investigators obtained subpoenas and warrants and reviewed thousands of communications, many on Discord, before making the arrest.
Canadian investigators have reviewed more than 90 statements from students, educators and first responders and continue to examine other online contacts, Rain said.
GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT COLT GRAY CHANGES PLEA TO GUILTY, NOW FACES LIFE IN PRISON
A screengrab from a video shows students exiting the Tumbler Ridge school after deadly shootings, in British Columbia, Canada, Feb. 10. (Jordon Kosik via AP, File)
"Our RCMP criminal investigation remains ongoing and the possibility of further charges being pursued in Canada remains under active consideration," he said.
Herrington warned that assisting a mass shooting from afar does not shield someone from prosecution.
"If you think you are safe from prosecution because you did not pull the trigger, or were not physically present at the scene of the crime, think again," he said.

"The FBI and our partners will use all of the considerable investigative tools at our disposal to hold accountable those who enable or assist in acts of mass violence."

The Feb. 10 attack killed eight victims, including five students, an educator and the shooter’s mother and 11-year-old stepbrother, according to Canadian authorities. Van Rootselaar was found dead inside the school from an apparent self-inflicted injury.

title: Christa Pike now conscious and talking after surviving 2 doses of lethal injection drug
summary: Christa Pike is awake and talking after surviving two doses of pentobarbital during Tennessee's failed execution attempt, her attorneys say.
story: 'Outnumbered' panel weighs in on the debate over Krista Pike's failed death penalty.
A Tennessee death row inmate is awake and talking after surviving two doses of a lethal injection drug during a failed execution, her attorneys said Tuesday.
Christa Pike continues to receive critical medical care following Tennessee’s attempt to execute her last Wednesday, her attorneys said in a statement posted on the Mercy for Christa website.
"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," the statement said.
They said Pike remains handcuffed and shackled to her hospital bed despite severe damage to her arms.
LAWYERS, EXPERTS URGE TENNESSEE GOVERNOR TO COMMUTE CHRISTA PIKE’S SENTENCE AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

An execution gurney is shown alongside a Tennessee Department of Correction booking photo of death row inmate Christa Pike. (Greg Smith/CORBIS/Corbis via Getty Images; Tennessee Department of Correction via AP)
"Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery," the statement said.

Her attorneys said Pike survived two complete rounds of lethal injection under Tennessee’s protocol despite their warnings about problems with her veins. They thanked first responders and hospital staff for her care and renewed their request for Tennessee’s governor to commute her sentence to life without parole.
Pike, now 50, was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at the Knoxville Job Corps Center.
LETHAL INJECTION SURVIVOR CHRISTA PIKE'S FORMER SATANIST BOYFRIEND COULD BE RELEASED IN 5 YEARS
Christa Gail Pike appears remotely from Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation for her hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tenn., on Aug. 11, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

Pike was 18 when she and two classmates lured Slemmer to a park, where they tortured her for nearly an hour before crushing her skull with a chunk of broken asphalt, former Knoxville Police Chief Phil Keith previously told Fox News Digital.
Pike kept a fragment of Slemmer’s skull as a trophy and showed it to classmates before her arrest.
TENNESSEE PRISON CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER FAILED EXECUTION AS FORMER US ATTORNEY TAPPED TO LEAD INDEPENDENT REVIEW
Christa Gail Pike is seen during her trial for the murder of Colleen A. Slemmer March 18, 1996, in Knox County Criminal Court. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
Pike is the first person in the modern U.S. death penalty era known to survive the administration of lethal injection drugs, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Pike’s attorneys have also filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence from the failed execution attempt. They plan to hold a press conference Wednesday following a Davidson County Chancery Court hearing scheduled to begin at 11 a.m. local time.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Delta Air Lines jet clips Air Canada plane on Los Angeles International Airport tarmac
summary: A Delta Air Lines jet taxiing at LAX clipped an Air Canada plane being towed to the gate. The FAA is investigating the incident; no injuries reported.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Delta Air Lines passenger jet on Tuesday struck an Air Canada aircraft being towed to its arrival gate just after it landed at Los Angeles International Airport, both airlines said.

Delta Air Lines Flight 7, slated to depart for Tokyo, carrying 275 passengers and 15 crew members, struck an Air Canada passenger jet with its left wingtip, a Delta spokesperson told Fox News Digital. No injuries were initially reported.

"While taxiing at Los Angeles International Airport, a Delta aircraft made contact with an Air Canada aircraft," a Delta statement said. "Nothing is more important than the safety of our customers and people, and we apologize to our customers for the experience and delay in their travel."
'WE NEED TO RETURN IMMEDIATELY,' FLIGHT CREW WARNS AS PILOT HEALTH EMERGENCY UNFOLDS
A Delta Air Lines flight takes off the tarmac. (iStock)
Air Canada flight AC785 had just arrived to Los Angeles from Toronto when it was being towed to the gate, the airline told Fox News Digital.

"An aircraft operated by another airline made contact with its tail," Air Canada said. "There are no reported injuries. The Air Canada aircraft will be taken out of service for inspection and repairs.
MAN SPARKS OUTRAGE BY CALLING 30-MINUTE AIRPORT RIDE FOR HIS WIFE A ‘MASSIVE INCONVENIENCE’
An Air Canada plane. (iStock)
A video posted online by TMZ shows an Air Canada plane with a visible gash on one of its wings.

No injuries were reported, the airline said. Delta maintenance crews and airport teams are assessing the aircraft, an Airbus A350-900. The airline said it was working to accommodate the passengers and was evaluating "recovery options."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The airline said it will cooperate with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which will investigate the incident.

In March, a regional Air Canada plane collided with a Port Authority airport vehicle at LaGuardia Airport in New York City. The collision destroyed the front of the aircraft and left two pilots dead and dozens injured.
This story is breaking. Please check back for updates.

title: Mother, son among six identified after Boston-bound medevac jet vanishes off Nantucket
summary: The six people aboard the Latitude Air Ambulance medevac jet that vanished over the Atlantic near Nantucket while en route to Boston have been identified.
story: The Coast Guard suspends the search for six people presumed dead after a medical plane plunged 13,000 feet in three minutes near Nantucket. Aviation attorney Jim Brauchle joins Brian Kilmeade to analyze the flight data.
The six people aboard a Boston-bound medical jet that disappeared over the Atlantic have been identified as a Bermudian mother and son and a four-person Canadian flight and medical crew.
Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, was being transported for treatment related to a stroke, with her son, Sergio Wayne Lottimore, accompanying her aboard the medevac flight.
The U.S. Coast Guard identified the four Canadians aboard as Philip Gregory Childerhose, Thomas Henry Farquhar, Sarah Jane Paton and Jolene Beth Weir.
1 MISSING, 4 RUSHED TO HOSPITAL AFTER HELICOPTER CRASHES OFF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ISLAND

Jolene Beth Weir, left, and Sergio Wayne Lottimore with his mother, Marilyn Lavonne Bean, were among six people aboard the Boston-bound medevac flight that disappeared off Nantucket. (Facebook/Mackenzie Weir; Facebook)
Childerhose was the captain and Farquhar was the first officer, while Paton served as the flight nurse and Weir as the respiratory therapist, according to Latitude Air Ambulance.

The Gulfstream G100 disappeared early Saturday while traveling from Bermuda to Boston, triggering a major Coast Guard search off Nantucket. The Coast Guard suspended the search Sunday after debris associated with the aircraft was located.
Lottimore was senior vice president and head of specialty reinsurance at Hamilton Re, according to the Bermuda-based company.
"The entire Hamilton team is heartbroken by the loss of a respected leader, colleague and friend," Hamilton Re said in a statement.
4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS
Sergio Wayne Lottimore, left, and his mother, Marilyn Lavonne Bean, were aboard the Boston-bound medevac flight that disappeared off Nantucket. (Facebook)
Lottimore was also a 2002 graduate of Warwick Academy, where he had served as a prefect. The school remembered him as an "outstanding person."
Bermuda Police said a family liaison officer had been assigned to assist the family.

The aircraft was operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, a Canadian medical transport company. Latitude previously confirmed to Fox News Digital that the Gulfstream was operating as a medevac flight and was expected to make the journey from Bermuda to Boston in approximately two hours.
Latitude Air Ambulance President Peter Byl said the company was mourning an "unimaginable loss."

"Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities," Byl said. "We will honour our colleagues by remembering the care, professionalism, and commitment they brought to their work every day."
The flight departed Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport late Friday night and was bound for Boston Logan International Airport.
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN ON BOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE
Jolene Beth Weir, a respiratory therapist aboard the missing Boston-bound medevac flight, poses for a photo with a dog. (Facebook/Mackenzie Weir)

The Transportation Safety Board of Canada said the crew reported electrical difficulties as the aircraft approached the Boston area before the jet descended rapidly and air traffic control lost contact south of Nantucket.
FlightAware data previously reviewed by Fox News Digital showed the aircraft descending from 24,000 feet to 11,000 feet in roughly three minutes around 1 a.m. Saturday.

The Federal Aviation Administration previously told Fox News Digital that it issued a Search and Rescue Alert Notice at approximately 1:20 a.m. ET. Massport later confirmed the aircraft never arrived at Boston Logan.
A civilian vessel located debris associated with the aircraft, according to the Coast Guard.

"During this incredibly difficult time, our heartfelt condolences go out to the families and friends impacted by this tragic incident," Rear Adm. Matthew Lake, commander of the Coast Guard Northeast District, said Monday.
"We are grateful to the crews and partner agencies who quickly responded to this incident, and we will continue to support our Canadian partners as they conduct their investigation," Lake added.

Canada is leading the investigation because the aircraft was registered there, in accordance with international agreements, according to the TSB. The National Transportation Safety Board is assisting as an accredited representative for the United States.

Authorities announced that DNA testing identified a body found in a Texas creek as a missing flight attendant whose roommate has been charged with killing her and dumping her remains off a bridge.

Day allegedly told investigators he strangled Soluri on the kitchen floor, dragged her body into the backyard, loaded her "head first" into a large black trash bin and transported her body roughly 70 miles away before dumping it over a bridge, according to court documents.

Investigators said home surveillance video from Day’s Fort Worth house showed him dragging "what appears to be a lifeless body from the home into the backyard" on March 21, 2025. title: Cornell protesters swarm campus to support Jane Doe, call for university president's resignation
summary: Cornell University faculty push a no confidence vote as student protests erupt over sexual assault allegations tied to a fraternity lawsuit.
story: Criminal defense attorney Josh Ritter discusses protests at Cornell University as students push back against the administration's handling of a sexual assault investigation. Ritter also discusses evidence in the case and what the prosecution must prove.
Faculty at Cornell University are weighing a vote of no confidence in the school's administration as student protesters take over the campus in response to sexual assault allegations on Tuesday.
The no-confidence resolution has secured support from 40 of the faculty senate's 75 voting members, according to the resolution's sponsor, professor Paul Ortiz.

"As you may suspect, we were approached in our capacity as faculty senators by numerous Cornell colleagues demanding action. Many of these faculty – including myself – were approached by students at Cornell who are upset, fearful for their personal safety, and wanting our university to address the perennial problem of sexual assault on the campus," Ortiz wrote.
AOC'S DRAMATIC RETELLING OF CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS COLLIDES WITH COMPLAINT DETAILS

Students protest on Ho Plaza at Cornell University, Monday Oct. 5, 2026, in Ithaca, N.Y., in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024, accused are some members of the Chi Phi fraternity. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)
Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff also faced questions from the student body during a campus assembly on Monday as protests took over the college.

"We’re not hiding anything at Cornell," Kotlikoff told students, according to the Cornell Daily Sun student newspaper. "You will hear proposals from us going forward around what we’re going to do to try and improve this culture and address this problem."
Kotlikoff has so far dismissed student calls for his resignation.
CORNELL CAMPUS POLICE MADE DRUG ARREST AT CHI PHI FRATERNITY HOUSE HOURS BEFORE ALLEGED GANG RAPE
Students protest on Ho Plaza at Cornell University, Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 in Ithaca, N.Y. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in a lawsuit of drugging and raping a female Cornell student during a night of drinking, drugs and group sex at their fraternity house in October 2024.

The accuser, identified in court papers by the pseudonym Jane Doe, alleges the men sexually assaulted her after she arrived intoxicated and was pressured into taking ketamine and other substances. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated in it. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.
ATTORNEY FOR ACCUSED CORNELL STUDENT CALLS ON LETITIA JAMES TO STEP ASIDE OVER PRIOR COMMENTS
Students protest at Cornell University, Monday, Oct. 5, 2026. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

The case has now erupted into a political and legal firestorm, with New York Attorney General Letitia James announcing Friday that her office is conducting an "active criminal investigation" after Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed the Office of the Attorney General as special prosecutor. Cornell has separately agreed to retain outside counsel to conduct an independent review of the university's handling of the allegations.

At the center of the controversy are sharply conflicting accounts of what happened that night, including differences between what Doe said in the weeks afterward, what prosecutors say they received from Cornell police and the explosive allegations contained in a lawsuit filed nearly two years later.
Students protest at Cornell University, Monday Oct. 5, 2026, in Ithaca, N.Y. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said Doe's November 2024 sworn statement did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."

title: Atlanta robbery suspect allegedly steals police cruiser, crashes into tanker truck
summary: Phelan Thorpe allegedly stole a marked Atlanta police cruiser and crashed it into a tanker truck on I-675 while wanted for a Midtown MARTA robbery.
story: A man in Atlanta attacked a woman in broad daylight Saturday, before stealing a police cruiser and crashing into a tanker truck, police said. (Atlanta Police Department)

A man wanted in connection with the violent robbery of a woman near an Atlanta transit station was arrested Monday after allegedly stealing a marked police cruiser and crashing it into a tanker truck, authorities said.
Atlanta police identified the suspect as 30-year-old Phelan Thorpe, who investigators say was wanted in connection with a Saturday afternoon robbery near the Midtown MARTA station.
Thorpe was charged with robbery and simple battery in connection with the alleged attack, according to the Atlanta Police Department.

Officers were dispatched shortly after 5:15 p.m. Monday to the 2000 block of Thomasville Drive SE after receiving a report that a wanted man was at the location and possibly armed, according to police.
MAN FACING FEDERAL CHARGES AFTER ATLANTA TRAIN PASSENGER STABBED ABOUT 20 TIMES, FBI INVESTIGATING

Video released by the Atlanta Police Department shows a suspect following a woman from the Midtown MARTA station before allegedly attacking and robbing her near 10th and West Peachtree streets on Oct. 3, 2026. (Atlanta Police Department)
Officers located Thorpe and began investigating, but police said he managed to get into a marked Atlanta Police Department patrol vehicle parked outside and drive away.
Thorpe allegedly drove the cruiser into neighboring Clayton County before crashing into a tanker truck on Interstate 675.
SUSPECTED DUI DRIVER LEADS COPS ON WILD CHASE BEFORE DRAMATIC TAKEDOWN ON POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH

He was taken into custody after the crash without further incident. Thorpe suffered minor, non-life-threatening injuries and was taken to a hospital, police said. No officers or other civilians were reported injured.
The woman who was attacked and robbed near the Midtown MARTA station gathers herself in the aftermath of the Oct. 3, 2026, mugging in Atlanta. (Atlanta Police Department)
Police had been looking for Thorpe in connection with an attack Saturday near 10th Street and West Peachtree Street in Midtown Atlanta.
Officers responded at approximately 1:54 p.m. and found a woman who had been injured during an assault and robbery, according to police.
FLORIDA MAN IN 'NO CHRIST NO LIFE' T-SHIRT CAUGHT ON VIDEO ALLEGEDLY ATTACKING, ROBBING WOMAN, 82, AT BUS STOP

Investigators said a man had followed the woman from the Midtown MARTA station before confronting her and claiming he had a gun. Police said the suspect demanded the woman's purse and iPhone, leading to a physical struggle.

The suspect allegedly punched the woman with a closed fist before taking her phone and driver's license, then fleeing the scene, according to police. The woman was transported to a hospital for evaluation.
Surveillance video released by Atlanta police showed a man following the woman near a crosswalk before the confrontation. Police had initially asked the public for help identifying him.
An Atlanta police cruiser. (atlantaga.gov)
Atlanta police later identified Thorpe as the suspect wanted in connection with the robbery and said he was charged with robbery and simple battery.
It was not immediately clear how Thorpe allegedly gained access to the patrol vehicle or whether police recovered a firearm.
A police update Monday night did not identify any charges stemming from the alleged theft of the patrol vehicle or subsequent crash.

title: Jim Bakker, 'PTL Club' televangelist and fmr husband of Tammy Faye, dead at 86
summary: Televangelist Jim Bakker, the host of the popular “The PTL Club" TV show with his former wife Tammy Faye Bakker, died Monday at the age of 86.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Televangelist Jim Bakker, who rose to fame with the "The PTL Club" TV show before admitting to a sexual encounter with a church clerk and being convicted of financial crimes, has died at the age of 86.
Bakker's second wife, Lori, said Jim passed away on Monday. His cause of death is unclear, and it comes after Bakker suffered a stroke in 2020.

"It is with a broken heart that I share that my beloved husband, Jim Bakker, went home to be with the Lord this evening," Lori Bakker said in a statement. "For 66 years, Jim gave his life to preaching the Gospel of Jesus Christ. He was a pioneer of Christian television, but to me, he was my husband, my best friend, and the man I was honored to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry.

"Jim loved people deeply. He loved this ministry, and he loved the friends and partners who stood with him throughout the years. Even in his final days, his heart was still for the work of God and for the Gospel to continue reaching the world," she added.
NOAH'S ARK MYSTERY ENTERS NEW PHASE AS RESEARCHERS PROBE DEEP BENEATH SITE
Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker speak to their television audience on Aug. 20, 1986, at their PTL Ministry in Fort Mill, S.C. (Lou Krasky/AP)

Bakker was born in Muskegon, Michigan, and attended North Central Bible College in Minneapolis, where he met his first wife, Tammy Faye. They married in 1961 and dropped out of college to start their own traveling ministry. He preached, while she sang and played the accordion as they crossed the country, visiting churches and tent revivals.

"In the 1960s, he joined the Christian Broadcasting Network under the direction of Pat Robertson. Jim developed one of the first daily, one-hour, kids’ shows for Christians called 'Come On Over,'" read a biography of Bakker on his website. "He also later became the first host of a ground-breaking talk show called 'The 700 Club,' featuring many of the top ministers and singers of the day."
Bakker then left CBN in 1972 and two years later formed the PTL Satellite Network. "The PTL Club" — with PTL standing for "Praise the Lord" — became its signature show.

During the peak of its popularity in the 1980s, "The PTL Club" was drawing millions of viewers and bringing in millions of dollars annually from followers, according to The Associated Press. The show was based around chats with guests and Christian entertainers, with Bakker offering upbeat sermons and Tammy Faye singing.
Their ministry also included the Christian-based Heritage USA theme park and hotel in Fort Mill, South Carolina.
FULTON SHEEN BECAME A TV SENSATION PREACHING FAITH, MORALITY AND WARNINGS MICHAEL KNOWLES SAYS STILL RESONATE
Jim and Tammy Bakker enjoy a night on the town as they arrive at the Beverly Theatre on Oct. 24, 1987, to see "The Gospel Truth." (Douglas C. Pizach/AP)

However, Bakker's empire began to unravel in March 1987 when he admitted to a sexual encounter with church clerk Jessica Hahn, forcing him to turn over operations to pastor and broadcaster Jerry Falwell.

In 1988, Bakker was indicted for mail fraud, wire fraud and conspiracy after an investigation of PTL’s finances. He was convicted and sentenced to 45 years in federal prison, though the sentence was later reduced to eight years.
At a news conference after Bakker was found guilty, Tammy Faye stood in front of the microphones and sang the hymn, "On Christ the Solid Rock I Stand," the AP reported.

Tammy Faye then divorced Bakker in 1992 while he was still in prison. She married Roe Messner, a building contractor whose projects included the Heritage USA theme park. Messner spent about two years in prison after being convicted of bankruptcy fraud in 1995, while Tammy Faye later died of colon cancer in 2007.
Bakker, meanwhile, was released on parole in 1995 and married Lori in 1998. The couple launched "The Jim Bakker Show" on the PTL Satellite Network five years later.

"The Jim Bakker Show is an hour-long daily broadcast featuring prophetic and Biblical revelations brought to light in today’s world. In these end times God is providing answers and wisdom to be revealed at just the right time. And the time is now!" the show says on its website.
Bakker and Tammy Faye had two children. He and his second wife adopted five children in 2002.
U.S. marshals escort former PTL leader Jim Bakker from his attorney's office to a waiting car in Charlotte, N.C., on Aug. 31, 1989. (Chuck Burton/AP)
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

The Associated Press also reported that in June 2021, Bakker and his Morningside Church Productions Inc. settled a lawsuit accusing him of falsely claiming the health supplement Silver Solution could cure COVID-19. The settlement called for $156,000 in refunds to people who paid money or gave contributions to obtain the product in the early days of the pandemic.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Kentucky bourbon CEO fired after lawsuit alleges hidden cameras recording family members, minors nude: reports
summary: Wes Henderson allegedly hid about 15 cameras disguised as fire alarms, clocks and chargers at homes and The Kentucky Castle resort in Versailles.
story: Michael Balboni, former Homeland Security advisor for New York state and cyber security expert, said hidden cameras can be found anywhere, like smoke detectors or stuffed animals.

Kentucky bourbon executive Wes Henderson lost his job earlier this month after family members accused him of using hidden cameras to record relatives and guests at his homes and a castle resort, according to reports.
TKC Distilling, the parent company of The Kentucky Castle and True Story Whiskey, terminated Henderson as CEO Oct. 3.
Relatives filed the lawsuit against Henderson in Oldham County, Kentucky, in June, according to The Courier Journal, which obtained the now-sealed complaint.

Wes Henderson, Angel's Envy chief innovations officer at the time, attends the Unbridled Eve Gala during the 144th Kentucky Derby at Galt House Hotel & Suites on May 4, 2018, in Louisville, Ky. (Getty Images for Unbridled Eve)
RUTGERS RESEARCH DEAN ACCUSED OF SECRETLY RECORDING 'UPSKIRT' VIDEOS WITH CELLPHONE, PROSECUTORS SAY
Now, the Department of Homeland Security is examining hidden recordings Henderson allegedly made, the Lexington Herald-Leader reported. Fox News Digital reached out to DHS for comment.

"Wes unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit," Henderson's attorney said in a statement, according to the Herald-Leader. "It is our understanding that the complaint will be voluntarily dismissed. If that does not happen, he is prepared to vigorously defend himself."

Family members alleged that they discovered concealed cameras during a June 2025 stay at Henderson’s vacation home near Melbourne, Florida. They said they removed about 15 cameras, including devices disguised as fire alarms. They also found cameras hidden in a fan, a clock, a speaker, charging blocks and outlet extenders.
WEST VIRGINIA PRINCIPAL SUSPENDED AFTER RECORDING DEVICES FOUND IN GIRLS’ LOCKER ROOMS
They also reportedly found a camera hidden in a bathroom air vent and footage showing Henderson positioning a camera in front of a bed.

The complaint described footage of guests changing clothes and using bathrooms while unknowingly being recorded, along with people engaged in sexual acts. Some recordings allegedly showed Henderson, who is married, having sex with other women.
SEN LANKFORD ACCUSES PORNHUB OF 'PREYING ON CHILDREN' IN BLISTERING LETTER
The complaint also alleged that cameras recorded minors while they were nude. After reviewing some of the recordings, family members turned the evidence over to authorities.
According to the lawsuit, Henderson's wife later gave relatives permission to search the couple's Oldham County home, where additional hidden cameras had been installed.
WOMEN ACCUSE PEARADISE FOUNDER OF PREYING ON THEM BY TURNING ‘SAFE SPACE’ INTO MANSION OF MANIPULATION
Other memory cards allegedly held footage recorded at The Kentucky Castle in Versailles, Kentucky, owned by Henderson.
Kentucky Castle in Lexington, Kentucky. (Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

The lawsuit reportedly identified 40 people who appeared in the recordings without their knowledge or consent, including an alleged homeless person carrying what appeared to be a medical device into a restroom.
The plaintiffs are seeking damages for pain and suffering and medical expenses. They have requested a jury trial, according to the Courier Journal.

Charity Bird, an attorney for TKC Distilling, told Fox News Digital the company is not a party to the lawsuit and that Henderson's son, Kyle Henderson, will take over as CEO of The Kentucky Castle and True Story Whiskey.

"The Board and leadership of TKC Distilling, the parent company of The Kentucky Castle and True Story Whiskey, have terminated the employment of CEO Wes Henderson, effective immediately, in light of allegations outlined in a recently filed lawsuit," Bird said in an emailed statement.

Henderson's attorney denied the allegations in a statement to the Herald-Leader. The attorney said Henderson expected the plaintiffs to drop the case, but would fight the allegations if they continued to pursue it.
Wes Henderson attends the 145th Kentucky Derby Unbridled Eve Gala at The Galt House Hotel & Suites Grand Ballroom in Louisville, Ky., on May 3, 2019. (Getty Images for Unbridled Eve)
Separately, TKC Distilling and related businesses have faced lawsuits over allegedly unpaid architectural and consulting bills.
Henderson, a former firefighter, recently took a leave of absence as the Oldham County deputy coroner, Oldham County Coroner David Pendleton told the Courier Journal.
Meanwhile, the exact location of the recordings and devices remains unclear.

title: Ole Miss students, bar workers warn of culture of underage drinking, fake ID schemes and frat allegations
summary: Fox News Digital investigates nightlife in Oxford, Mississippi, where students and local bartenders reveal how easy it is to exploit bar entry policies and bypass security checks.
story: Ole Miss students and bar workers in Oxford, Mississippi, warned of a rampant underage drinking culture in the college town.
FIRST ON FOX: OXFORD, Miss. – "It's rampant for sure."
That is how Reagan Fiser, a local bartender who has worked in Oxford nightlife for nearly seven years, describes the sheer volume of underage Ole Miss students slipping into bars around "The Square."

It's a bustling college town watering hole hub packed with historic storefronts, crowded balconies and high-volume drinking establishments just a mile away from the University of Mississippi's campus.

An extensive investigation by Fox News Digital, backed by interviews with more than 30 students, bartenders and venue employees, reveals an environment where underage drinking thrives around The Square, with students and nightlife workers describing fake IDs, ID sharing and other low-tech methods used to skirt age restrictions.
Oxford, Mississippi is a hub for nightlife for Ole Miss students. (Fox News; John Korduner/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
OXFORD MAYOR WARNS KRATOM IS 'ROLLING THE DICE ON DEATH' AS FEARS LINGER OVER OLE MISS DEATHS

Oxford Mayor Robyn Tannehill and Police Chief Jeff McCutchen, responding to Fox News Digital's reporting, said the city takes underage drinking, fraudulent identification, illegal drug use and the safety of students, residents and visitors seriously.

"We are not suggesting that underage drinking, fake identification, illegal drugs or other safety concerns do not exist in Oxford. Our own enforcement numbers demonstrate that these challenges are real," Tannehill said in a joint statement with McCutchen.

Those numbers include 759 false identification cards confiscated, 378 alcohol-possession-by-a-minor violations and 98 fake-ID citations during the calendar-year reporting period, according to Oxford Police.
Oxford City Hall is located within "The Square." (Kelsie Cairns)
Underage drinking in Oxford is neither hidden nor isolated.

One sophomore student verified that getting a fake ID comes down to basic word-of-mouth networking, emphasizing that the culture spans the entire campus: "I think it's everyone, it's everyone ... like every student, no matter if you're in a sorority or fraternity."
POLICE NEAR OLE MISS RESPOND TO SUSPECTED OVERDOSE, SAY 'NOT STUDENT-RELATED'
Ole Miss flags hang in The Square. (Kelsie Cairns)
"Depending on what year you are, depends on what bar you go to," another female freshman explained.
Fiser identified certain bars as "upperclassmen bars" catering to older crowds, while venues operating under Mississippi's 18-plus model serve as magnets for younger students, she said.
THE FRAT OMERTÀ: WHISTLEBLOWER WARNS OF ‘CODE OF SILENCE’ AFTER OLE MISS DEATHS, ALLEGED PENN STATE COKE RING
Reagan Fiser, a local bartender in Oxford, Mississippi, addresses the underage drinking culture in her community. (Kelsie Cairns)
While venues mark minors with stamps and patrons older than 21 with wristbands, industry insiders said enforcement collapses in crowded rooms.
One bartender mentioned an establishment that serves under-21 crowds "all the time."
Fiser added that cheap drink promotions at 18-plus venues create a volatile mix: "Their whole concept is like cheap drinks ... That feels a little sticky."
Fans flocked to Oxford ahead of the LSU versus Ole Miss showdown on Sept. 19, 2026. (Trey Wallace/OutKick)
Getting past door security rarely requires complex methods; patrons routinely rely on simple hand-offs and ID sharing in line.

"I've heard stories of people passing around the same fake, just ... back to the person behind them, and it's working because people don't pay attention," Fiser told Fox News Digital. "And a lot of people don't [try to hide it] because they know they'll get away with it."

Local bouncer Haj Bah confirmed catching ID-sharers in real time outside the bar where he works, denying entry to three underage patrons Friday evening — including a pair caught sharing an ID in line.It all happened just moments before his interview with Fox News Digital.
VAPE STORE CLERKS NEAR OLE MISS CAMPUS JAILED, FACING DRUG CHARGES
A security officer outside flagged a patron handing an ID to another person waiting behind him.
Local bouncer Haj Bah describes his nightly battle with fake IDs in Oxford, Mississippi. (Kelsie Cairns)
"As soon as they came up, I said, 'No.' And for that person who passed the ID over, we asked that person to leave too," Bah said.
He went on to say, "Giving that fake ID is the same as a bartender giving alcohol to the child. In my eyes, that is the same thing."

While bouncers work to intercept hand-offs, freshman student Drew Ferra noted "how easy" it can be to get served under 21, but argued that venue owners shouldn't bear full blame when patrons present "fakes."
OLE MISS TOXICOLOGY REPORTS EXPECTED SOON AND RESULTS MAY TRIGGER ANTI-FENTANYL LAW, OFFICIAL SAYS

"The bars here are very strict, but if you have a fake ID, I feel like you can’t blame the bar," Ferra said. "You’re presenting them something that proves you’re 21. In my opinion, should you do it? No. It’s gonna happen though, right?"

Ole Miss freshman Drew Ferra confirms to Fox News Digital that underage drinking is prevalent in Oxford, Mississippi, bars, but maintains bouncers are strict to let underage people into places that serve booze around town. (Kelsie Cairns)
Meanwhile, some long-standing Oxford establishments were praised by sources for aggressive vetting.
"Their bouncers are very trained on what to look for," Fiser noted. "There is a reason why I feel like those places have lasted."

A New York City Police Department detective was released from the hospital after he was stabbed multiple times during a robbery in the Bronx last week, according to officials.
Detective Jose Mercedes was wheeled out of Jacobi Medical Center in Morris Park on Monday before standing up in front of a group of clapping officers.

"Today, in another incredible feat of strength and determination, Detective Mercedes got up from his wheelchair and walked out of Jacobi Medical Center on his own two feet. Hundreds of members of the NYPD were there to cheer their brother on," Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said on X.
NYPD DETECTIVE, CHILDREN SHOT IN SEPARATE BROOKLYN SHOOTINGS OVER HOLIDAY WEEKEND
Detective Jose Mercedes was wheeled out of Jacobi Medical Center in Morris Park on Monday before standing up in front of a group of clapping officers. (NYPD)
"The entire department stands behind Detective Mercedes as he continues his recovery. And the greatest detectives in the world will relentlessly pursue those responsible for this crime," she added.

Mercedes was off-duty when two suspects on an e-bike attempted to snatch his gold chain as he was clearing out the trunk of his car in the Norwood neighborhood on Friday afternoon, according to officials.

The two attackers remain at large. (NYPD)

The detective attempted to fight back, but he was stabbed and slashed seven times during the struggle before the assailants fled. Authorities said the confrontation began when the men attempted to steal his gold chain.
Mercedes then pursued the fleeing attackers on foot for about two blocks before collapsing near East 206th Street and Rochambeau Avenue.
"Despite his serious injuries, Detective Mercedes chased after his attackers on foot," Tisch said.

title: Massachusetts felon pleads guilty after DOJ says he sold Russian plutonium to 67 customers
summary: A convicted felon from Massachusetts pleaded guilty to illegally importing plutonium from Russia and selling it to customers in the U.S. and abroad.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A convicted felon from Massachusetts has pleaded guilty to illegally importing plutonium from Russia and selling the radioactive material and other highly toxic and hazardous materials to customers in the U.S. and abroad, while also pleading guilty to possessing child sexual abuse material.

Jacob D. Miller, 44, pleaded guilty to one count of being a felon in possession of ammunition, one count of being a felon in possession of explosive materials, one count of importing nuclear material without lawful authority, one count of mailing hazardous materials and one count of possession of child pornography, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Massachusetts.
Miller was arrested on April 9, 2025, and indicted by a grand jury on April 17. He has remained in federal custody since his arrest.
US REMOVES RADIOACTIVE CANCER-TREATMENT MATERIAL FROM CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRY OVER 'DIRTY BOMB' RISK
A convicted felon has pleaded guilty to illegally importing plutonium from Russia and selling it to customers in the U.S. and abroad. (FBI Boston:DOJ)

He had previously been convicted on Feb. 9, 2004, in Massachusetts state court for possessing child pornography and possessing an explosive device. According to federal prosecutors, Miller received seven years of probation in the child pornography case and, in a separate case involving two counts of possessing an explosive device, was sentenced to 2½ years in jail and 10 years of probation.

After his release, Miller started a business called Collect The Periodic Table (CTPT) and sold samples of elements such as plutonium, which is highly radioactive, and thallium, which is highly toxic, according to prosecutors. In addition to selling through CTPT directly, Miller used an online third-party retailer, Bonanza, to make sales.

Miller imported plutonium from Russia and arranged for it to be mailed to him at his Massachusetts residence, prosecutors said. Between Dec. 30, 2020, and March 31, 2025, Miller sold plutonium to about 67 customers across the U.S. and abroad. Miller shipped the plutonium to his customers through a U.S. mail service, despite plutonium being a hazardous substance that was prohibited from being shipped.
A box of Federal American Eagle .45-caliber ammunition. Miller pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of ammunition. (FBI Boston)

Between Oct. 12, 2017, and April 5, 2025, Miller used CTPT and Bonanza to sell thallium to about 71 customers, according to prosecutors. Miller also shipped the thallium to his customers through the U.S. mail, even though thallium was also a hazardous substance that was barred from being mailed.

During a search of Miller’s residence in April 2025, a box containing bottles of explosive powder, numerous rounds of ammunition and six firearms were recovered by investigators. The ammunition, firearms and explosive materials were unlawfully possessed because of his previous felony convictions, prosecutors said.
FORMER NORTH TEXAS POLICE OFFICER GIVEN THREE LIFE SENTENCES FOR CHILD PORNOGRAPHY, SOLICITATION OF MINOR
Federal investigators seized .45-caliber ammunition during a search of Jacob D. Miller’s Massachusetts residence in April 2025. (FBI Boston)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Miller’s laptop and cell phone were also found with child sexual abuse materials that he had opened as recently as the day before the search warrant, according to prosecutors.
His sentencing has been scheduled for Jan. 21.

title: Nobu chef killed after teen driver crashes into parked car in California
summary: A longtime chef at Nobu Malibu was napping in his parked car before his shift when a speeding 16-year-old slammed his Range Rover into his sedan.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A longtime chef at Nobu Malibu in California was killed when a teenage driver crashed into his parked car as he was sleeping.
Ryo Uchimiya, 51, was a sushi chef who had worked at the famous Japanese restaurant for 25 years, according to KTLA.

Uchimiya was parked at the curb and napping in his car before starting his shift on Saturday morning when a 16-year-old boy plowed his Range Rover into the rear of the chef's parked sedan at around 6:50 a.m.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said the teenager appeared to be speeding when he slammed his SUV into Uchimiya, according to KTLA. Investigators said there was no indication that the teenager was driving under the influence.
FLORIDA WOMAN ACCUSED OF DUI CRASHES SUV INTO PARKED CAR, THEN MAKES BIZARRE PLEA TO POLICE CAUGHT ON CAMERA
A longtime chef at Nobu Malibu in California was killed when a teenage driver crashed into his parked car as he was sleeping. (Google Maps)
It remains unclear whether the teenager will face any charges as the incident remains under investigation.

Uchimiya died from "multiple blunt force injuries," according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office, the New York Post reported. The medical examiner also ruled the manner of death an accident.
Surveillance footage showed the driver's SUV slamming into Uchimiya’s parked car, causing a chain-reaction crash that pushed the sedan into two other vehicles in front of him.
A witness told KTLA that the teenage driver appeared to be shocked and confused after the collision.
SILICON VALLEY DEVELOPER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER INVESTIGATORS SAY TESLA REACHED 142 MPH BEFORE FATAL CRASH
Ryo Uchimiya, 51, was a sushi chef who had worked at the famous Japanese restaurant for 25 years. (Google Maps)

"I heard throughout the day that maybe he didn’t even have a license," she said. "He’s a young kid. He looked very young and very confused and his parents didn’t even show up to find him. He was sitting there for two hours by himself."

People who work and live near the restaurant said the stretch of Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) where the deadly crash took place has a reputation for being dangerous, as drivers are constantly seen speeding, according to the outlet.

The Malibu City Council declared a local emergency in November 2023 over dangerous conditions on PCH, weeks after a speeding driver struck and killed four Pepperdine University students along the highway.
Uchimiya's loved ones and coworkers remembered him as a beloved husband, father of two children and talented chef, according to KTLA.
The manager of Nobu Malibu said the "family of staffers" at the restaurant are doing what they can to support Uchimiya’s family during this difficult time.
The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said the teenager appeared to be speeding. (Photo by Qian Weizhong/VCG via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Obviously, it’s been a very, very difficult day for so many people," the manager told the outlet.
"He was a real nice guy, very talented chef," a fellow Nobu chef told the New York Post. "It’s such a shame."
"He was resting, getting ready for a catering gig," the chef added. "We all get here really early."
A Nobu hostess told the outlet that staff members were still processing the loss.
"We’re not ready to talk about it now," she said. "We all need time."

title: Luxury fashion designers found shot dead in California as family reportedly reveals troubling lead-up
summary: Fashion designers Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found shot dead outside their California home as relatives reportedly revealed troubling details about the days before their deaths.
story: Aerial video shows police at the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2. Credit: KTVU
The husband and wife behind a California luxury clothing brand were found shot dead outside their hillside home, as relatives reportedly revealed troubling details about the days before their deaths.

Oakland police confirmed to Fox News Digital that Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were the two people found dead on Oct. 2 in the 400 block of Panoramic Way. The couple founded women’s luxury apparel company Bryn Walker.
Min’s brother, Paul Min, told the Los Angeles Times he believes Walker fatally shot his sister before turning the gun on himself. Police have not confirmed that account.
"This remains an active and ongoing investigation. No additional details are being provided at this time," Oakland police told Fox News Digital.
KANSAS CONVICTED FELON, SEX OFFENDER ALLEGEDLY KILLS FELLOW FAMILY MEMBERS BEFORE TAKING HIS OWN LIFE: POLICE
Police vehicles outside the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
A bouquet and handwritten closure notice appear outside a Bryn Walker storefront after the luxury clothing brand’s founders were found dead outside their Oakland home. (KTVU)
Paul Min described a troubling decline in his brother-in-law after he allegedly lost millions of dollars in risky financial ventures, according to the outlet.

He called Walker the "most honest, responsible, hardworking guy you have ever known" and struggled to reconcile the suspected violence with the man he had known and loved for nearly four decades, the outlet reported.
TIKTOK INFLUENCER WHO ACCUSED ESTRANGED HUSBAND OF PEDOPHILIA FOUND DEAD IN POSSIBLE MURDER-SUICIDE
An aerial view of the Panoramic Hill neighborhood, where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead outside their home Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Min said he and his sister agreed Walker needed psychiatric help after Walker allegedly suggested that the three of them "end things."
Michelle Min was planning to have her husband admitted for psychiatric treatment on the day of the shooting, her brother told the outlet.
‘MARVELOUS MRS. MAISEL’ SET DECORATOR SLAIN, HUSBAND FOUND DEAD IN FAMILY ALREADY SCARRED BY HOME KILLING
A police officer handles yellow tape near the scene where Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead in Oakland on Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Police have not confirmed the family’s claims about Walker’s mental health, financial losses or a possible motive.

Berkeley officers responded to Panoramic Way shortly after 10:30 a.m. Friday and found a man and woman suffering from gunshot wounds, KTLA reported. Officers attempted lifesaving measures until paramedics arrived, but the couple was pronounced dead at the scene.
Oakland police, the lead investigating agency, recovered a gun and had not ruled out murder-suicide or determined who fired the weapon, the Los Angeles Times reported.
FATHER-IN-LAW OF TRANS NYT EXEC ADMITTED KILLING HIM, WORKED 'IN CONCERT' WITH MOTHER-IN-LAW: DOCS
A Bryn Walker storefront in Berkeley, California. The brand’s founders, Bryan Walker and Michelle Min, were found dead outside their Oakland home Oct. 2, 2026. (Google Maps)
The couple met in Kansas in the 1980s before following Min’s parents to California and eventually building their Berkeley clothing business, according to the LA Times.

Bryn Walker has been based in Berkeley since 1992 and designs and produces its clothing in the San Francisco Bay Area, according to the company’s website. The brand says it operates six company-owned stores and supplies roughly 1,000 boutiques nationwide.
Its store directory lists two Berkeley locations and a shop in Vineyard Haven, Massachusetts, on Martha’s Vineyard.
Police gather outside the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Fox News Digital also reached out to Berkeley police for comment.

title: Convicted child predator allegedly attacks two women inside Planet Fitness women's locker room

story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A convicted child rapist allegedly attacked a woman after bringing her to a Planet Fitness gym to use the showers, then allegedly sexually assaulted an employee who tried to intervene.

Laquan Holland, 40, allegedly beat the woman, tried to strip off her clothing and blocked her escape inside the Cambridge, Massachusetts, gym, the Middlesex District Attorney’s Office told Fox News Digital.
The attack came weeks after a charge accusing Holland of failing to register as a sex offender was dismissed on the condition that he complete his registration, prosecutors confirmed.
Holland was ordered held without bail after his arraignment on two counts of assault to rape, two counts of indecent assault and battery, kidnapping and witness intimidation.
MICHIGAN DECISION FORCES REMOVAL OF DISGRACED SPORTS DOCTOR LARRY NASSAR FROM SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY
Laquan Holland, 40, is accused of sexually assaulting two women inside the women’s locker room at this Planet Fitness in Cambridge’s Porter Square on Oct. 1, 2026. (Google Maps)
A dangerousness hearing is scheduled for Oct. 16. NBC10 Boston reported that a not guilty plea was entered on his behalf.
Prosecutors said Holland, a member of the Porter Square gym, arrived around 9 a.m. Oct. 1 with a woman he knew after offering to let her use the showers.
But once they arrived, Holland allegedly began hitting her.
CALIFORNIA DEMS TRIGGER OUTRAGE AFTER SIDING WITH CONVICTED CHILD SEX OFFENDERS IN SHOCKING VOTE

The woman fled into the women’s locker room and shower area, authorities said. Holland allegedly followed, continuing to hit and touch her inappropriately while trying to remove her clothing and preventing her from leaving, according to the DA’s office.
WASHINGTON MOTHER SAYS SHE FOUND ADULT MALE SHOWERING IN WOMEN'S LOCKER ROOM DURING CHILDREN'S SWIM MEET
A convicted child rapist allegedly attacked a woman at a Planet Fitness before sexually assaulting an employee who intervened. (Don Emmert/AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images)
A female employee entered the shower area and tried to pull Holland off the woman. He allegedly sexually assaulted her, too.
Police arrived to find Holland in the locker room trying to put his clothes back on, prosecutors said.
Holland’s criminal history includes guilty pleas in 2006 to two counts of child rape and one count of indecent assault and battery on a child under 14, Boston.com reported, citing court records.
REPEAT OFFENDER WITH 7 PRIOR CONVICTIONS ARRESTED 3 TIMES IN 12 DAYS OVER ALLEGED ATTACKS ON WOMEN
The suspect was held without bail after prosecutors said he attacked two women inside a Planet Fitness locker room. (Andrew H. Walker/Getty Images for Planet Fitness)
More recently, Cambridge police arrested him Aug. 25 for failing to register as a sex offender, a subsequent offense, according to police records reviewed by Fox News Digital.
The DA’s office said Holland, who is homeless and was known to stay in Cambridge and Boston, must complete registration and verification requirements every 30 days.

He showed up at Cambridge police headquarters to register Aug. 25 but was arrested because he was late, prosecutors said. The charge was later dismissed on the condition that he register, which he completed Aug. 27.
FEMALE VIRGINIA OFFICER SUES POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHARING LOCKER ROOM WITH BIOLOGICAL MALE

title: Christa Pike execution failure spares murderer who bailed victim out just to kill him
summary: Gary Wayne Sutton's Dec. 3 execution is on hold after Tennessee's botched lethal injection of Christa Pike prompted Gov. Bill Lee to halt deaths.
story: Botched lethal injection attempts leave Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike in critical condition, prompting the resignation of the state's prison chief. Gov. Bill Lee postpones all executions through 2026 as an independent review begins. UC Berkeley Law professor John Yoo analyzes the legal controversy and previews key cases as the Supreme Court prepares to kick off its new term.

The execution of a double murderer who bailed one of his victims out of jail only for the man to be shot dead — and then killed his sister when she went looking for him — has been put on hold after Tennessee's botched attempt to lethally inject Christa Pike for her role in the "satanic" torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995.
Gov. Bill Lee halted the death penalty across the state for the rest of the year — but there was only one scheduled, the Dec. 3 execution of convicted double murderer Gary Wayne Sutton.
His uncle and co-defendant, James Dellinger, died of natural causes on death row in 2023.
FORMER KNOXVILLE POLICE CHIEF SAYS INVESTIGATORS ARE STILL HAUNTED BY COLLEEN SLEMMER'S MURDER 31 YEARS LATER
Gary Wayne Sutton pictured in a mugshot taken on Nov. 11, 2025, at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Tennessee. (Tennessee Department of Correction)
Sutton has maintained his innocence — but in separate trials, he was convicted in the murders of Tommy Griffin and Connie Branam, a brother and sister who were killed on Feb. 21 and 22, 1992.

Sutton, who months earlier had beaten up Griffin's brother, went drinking with Dellinger and Griffin at a bar called Howie's Hideaway on Feb. 21, 1992, according to court records reviewed by Fox News Digital.
After they left, they got in a fight, and Sutton and Dellinger left Griffin on the roadside. He encountered a passing driver who flagged down a police officer, according to court documents.
CHRISTA PIKE'S BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTION TAKES FOCUS OFF VICTIM, JEOPARDIZES EXECUTION: FORMER POLICE CHIEF
Christa Gail Pike appears remotely from Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation for her hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tenn., on Aug. 11, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The responding officer reported that Griffin was "on the verge of tears" and shirtless with "scrapes and scratches" on his upper body and a cut behind his ear. Griffin claimed he had gotten into "an argument with some friends, who were not really his friends," according to court records.

He declined to give specifics and was arrested for public intoxication. Sutton and Dellinger showed up at the police station to bail him out around 8:30 p.m. and were told to come back later. They did at about 11:30 p.m., bringing a flannel shirt, according to court documents.
A half-hour later, witnesses reported hearing three gunshots in the area where his body would later be found. He'd suffered a shotgun blast to the head.

Emergency vehicles arrive at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, Tenn., on Sept. 30, 2026. Pike had not been declared dead when witnesses were asked to leave the room they were in. (Denny Simmons/The Tennessean/USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)
LAWYERS, EXPERTS URGE TENNESSEE GOVERNOR TO COMMUTE CHRISTA PIKE’S SENTENCE AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

The next day, Griffin's sister, Branam, went to Howie's Hideaway with Sutton and Dellinger. She told the server she was looking for her brother. Her body was later found in her scorched car — so badly burned that the forensic pathologist could not determine whether she had been alive when the fire started. Detectives did recover a .303 cartridge that matched a rifle found at Dellinger's home.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Sutton's supporters have criticized the case as circumstantial. It remains unclear who shot Griffin and how exactly Branam died.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
Sutton's execution was scheduled for Dec. 3 but has been put on pause due to the state's failure to carry out Pike's death sentence last week.
Pike's botched execution was the second in Tennessee this year after executioners couldn't find a suitable vein for fellow condemned inmate Tony Carruthers in May.
DEATH ROW INMATE UNCONSCIOUS ON VENTILATOR AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION FOR TEEN’S KILLING: ATTORNEYS
A split image shows Christa Pike at her murder trial in 1995, left, and Colleen Slemmer, the young woman she was convicted of torturing and killing, on the right. (Reuters)
GOT A TIP?

While what's next for Pike remains unclear as she is in an undisclosed hospital for treatment following two doses of lethal injection drugs that failed to kill her, Lee said Carruthers would not face execution again for at least a year after his scheduled death in May was canceled.

Pike, who was hospitalized in critical condition, is the first person to have survived the administration of lethal injection drugs, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit that tracks capital punishment across the U.S.

In 2014, an Oklahoma inmate named Clayton Lockett initially survived the injection but died of a heart attack while still inside the chamber, according to the center.
